_comment: Follow-up measurement rule table (Phase 3). pdm_core/recommendations.py evaluates each rule's named trigger predicate (code) against the analysis result and emits the matching RecommendedMeasurement. This config owns the *what-fires-what* (techniques, purposes, priorities, phrasing); the trigger primitives live in code. Classical discriminators seeded from analyst practice — verify against the user's own measurement playbook.

diagnosis_rules.technique: Triaxial (or repeat axial) velocity measurement at the same point
diagnosis_rules.purpose: A 1x line on a single radial channel is consistent with rotor imbalance AND with an axial-dominant misalignment or bent shaft; the two differ in the AXIAL proportion, which an unmeasured axial channel cannot supply. Re-measuring with the sensor axially at the same point resolves the differential directly, and is the cheaper first step before phase work.
Phase relationships across the coupling separate imbalance from misalignment and confirm the 1x/2x source that a single sensor cannot resolve.

diagnosis_rules.technique: Time-waveform capture with enveloping/PeakVue and a higher-resolution spectrum
diagnosis_rules.purpose: Demodulated envelope and a longer time record confirm or rule out an early-stage bearing defect when the spectral peak alone is marginal.

diagnosis_rules.technique: Synchronous-averaged (order-tracked) time-waveform capture with envelope demodulation
diagnosis_rules.purpose: The matched bearing frequency coincides with an integer shaft order, where a bearing defect cannot be separated from shaft-order content (misalignment, looseness, electrical, or a plain shaft harmonic). Order-synchronous averaging cancels the shaft-order lines and envelope demodulation isolates any true bearing impact, resolving whether the peak is a bearing defect at all.

diagnosis_rules.technique: High-resolution enveloping/PeakVue capture with a longer time record
diagnosis_rules.purpose: The matched bearing peak sits near the broadband noise floor, where an apparent tone is not distinguishable from spectral noise. Demodulated enveloping amplifies early bearing impacts and a longer record lifts a true defect above the floor, confirming or clearing the candidate.

diagnosis_rules.technique: Laser shaft-alignment verification and thermography across the coupling
diagnosis_rules.purpose: Confirms the alignment condition directly and checks for coupling heat before committing to a corrective outage.

diagnosis_rules.technique: 1x phase comparison at both bearings of the affected shaft, plus dial-indicator shaft runout
diagnosis_rules.purpose: A bent shaft and an axial-dominant misalignment produce the same dominant axial 1x line, and on a machine whose shafts are not joined there is nothing to align or thermograph. The discriminator is the shaft itself: 1x phase read at both bearings separates a bend from a balance problem and indicates where along the shaft it sits, and dial-indicator runout measures the bend directly before committing to a straightening or replacement outage.
Distinguishes mechanical looseness from a late-stage bearing defect, which can present overlapping harmonic content.
A natural-frequency check separates a structural resonance from a forced-vibration fault at the same frequency.

diagnosis_rules.technique: Motor current signature analysis (MCSA) with a coast-down capture
diagnosis_rules.purpose: Coast-down separates electrically-forced vibration (disappears with power) from mechanical sources; MCSA confirms rotor/stator faults.

severity_coverage._comment: Session A. Fired once when the reading's ISO zone is not_assessable (velocity absent, or present-but-implausible) -- the reduced-scope coverage follow-up that resolves severity WITHOUT touching the fault diagnosis. Deliberately NOT a data_quality_rule (those fire per gate check and would also fire on machine-off fixtures); recommendations.py gates this on the reading itself.

not_assessable.technique: Velocity measurement per ISO 20816 (10-1000 Hz broadband, mm/s RMS)
not_assessable.purpose: Establishes the ISO 20816-3 severity zone. Severity cannot be assessed from this reading -- velocity was not measured (acceleration-only) or was outside a plausible range -- while fault detection from the spectral/envelope evidence is unaffected.

data_quality_rules._comment: Fired per failing/warning data-quality check on the reading, so an insufficient-data report still names exactly what to re-collect.

machine_running.technique: Re-measure with the machine confirmed running under normal load
machine_running.purpose: Vibration amplitudes were below the running threshold — the machine appears to have been off or unloaded during capture.

configuring.technique: Re-capture after the sensor has exited configuration mode
configuring.purpose: The sensor was still configuring, so the reading is not a valid operating measurement.

spectrum_non_flat.technique: Verify sensor mounting and cabling, then re-capture
spectrum_non_flat.purpose: The spectrum was flat/dead, which usually indicates a disconnected or failed sensor rather than a healthy machine.

spectral_plateau.technique: Re-capture, and confirm the export was not amplitude-capped or post-processed
spectral_plateau.purpose: A run of spectral bins carried one identical amplitude, so the levels in that region were written by something other than the measurement (a cap, a quantiser, or a synthetic fill) and cannot be read as true levels. Session DQ-FLAGS: this deliberately no longer advises a sensor range/gain change -- the check was renamed from 'clipping' because a flat-topped SPECTRUM is not what sensor saturation produces (saturation raises the broadband floor and adds harmonics), so the old advice pointed at a cause this evidence cannot establish.

sensor_settling.technique: Allow the sensor to settle after mounting/power-up, then re-capture
sensor_settling.purpose: Amplitude falls steeply and monotonically away from DC across the lowest bins -- the signature of a sensor or charge amplifier still settling during the capture, which inflates low-frequency amplitudes.

ac_coupling_rolloff.technique: Re-capture with a sensor and coupling rated below the running speed, or measure displacement
ac_coupling_rolloff.purpose: The running speed sits at or below the AC-coupling corner, so a true 1x line is attenuated by the measurement chain itself and its amplitude reads low.

line_frequency_content.technique: Confirm sensor cable routing and grounding, and declare the supply frequency and pole count
line_frequency_content.purpose: A discrete line sits on a nominal supply frequency and is not a shaft order on this machine. The origin cannot be established from this reading alone -- separating supply pickup from real machine content needs the declared line frequency and pole count, or slip sidebands.

ski_slope.technique: Check mounting integrity and re-capture with an appropriate high-pass setting
ski_slope.purpose: A low-frequency 'ski-slope' artifact was present, typically from a loose mount, cabling, or sensor settling.

speed_sanity.technique: Confirm the machine's actual running speed and re-capture
speed_sanity.purpose: No spectral content was found near the stated running speed, so the recorded speed or the capture may be wrong.
